summary: IDF drone strike killed Rafah Brigade commander Abu Younis with four missiles targeting a displaced persons tent in Al-Mawasi, west of Khan Yunis. Iran conducted multiple missile launches from Bandar Lengeh and toward the Strait of Hormuz, plus a UAV launch from Omidiyeh Air Base. Israeli artillery shelled four locations in southern Lebanon while warplanes operated overhead and dropped flares over Shama.

sections.threat_assessment: Iran's simultaneous missile launches from Bandar Lengeh and toward the Strait of Hormuz, coupled with UAV deployment from Omidiyeh, signal a coordinated escalation in maritime and aerial posture. The reported IRGC mining of tankers in the Strait of Hormuz directly threatens global energy transit, while the alleged drone plot against US leadership indicates expanded targeting ambitions. Israel's multi-axis artillery campaign in southern Lebanon and precision drone strike in Gaza reflect sustained high-tempo operations across fronts. The convergence of Iranian proxy activity in Iraq (Jurf al-Sakhar) with direct Iranian kinetic actions suggests an integrated pressure campaign.
sections.regional_response: The UN's urgent appeal for fertilizer shipments through the Strait of Hormuz highlights international concern over secondary humanitarian impacts of maritime disruption. Iraq's investigation into fuel siphoning at a Kataib Hezbollah stronghold indicates Baghdad may be attempting to constrain IRGC-linked networks under domestic pressure. Israel's unity government overture to Eisenkot suggests political consolidation for prolonged conflict management. The US security enhancements for Trump and officials reflect credible threat perception of Iranian retaliation capabilities.
sections.intelligence_notes: The 120-second delayed reporting of Iranian missile/UAV launches from Bandar Lengeh and Omidiyeh suggests operational security protocols but also provides near-real-time tracking capability. The specific use of four missiles against a single tent target in Al-Mawasi indicates high-value target prioritization and munition expenditure willingness. Multiple distinct artillery locations in southern Lebanon (Wadi Al-Salouqi, Wadi Nahla, Zibqin, Wadi Al-Hajir) imply a broad front rather than localized engagement. The IRGC's public claim of downing an MQ-1 over Qeshm, absent US confirmation, may serve deterrence signaling.
